title: More cash in the lost wallet
hook: Would more money in a lost wallet make its return less likely?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Compare reported return outcomes by wallet condition without predicting an individual's honesty.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Compare reported return outcomes by wallet condition without predicting an individual's honesty.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy wallet table records 51 returns out of 100 versus a 40% reference rate. What is the absolute difference? Toy inputs A=[51, 100, 40]; B=[40, 100, 40].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[51, 40, 11], [40, 40, 0]]. Labels: Return %, Reference %, Difference pp.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The table’s difference is measured in percentage points. Dividing that difference by the reference rate would answer a different, relative-change question. Aggregate return rates cannot predict whether a particular finder is honest.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Returned=40, Wallets=100, Reference %=40. What is Difference pp? Answer: 0.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Returned=40, Wallets=100, Reference %=40. What is Difference pp?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Across 40 countries, wallets with more money were returned more often: about 40% with none, 51% with $13.45 (Cohn, Maréchal, Tannenbaum & Zünd, 2019).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Compare reported return outcomes by wallet condition without predicting an individual's honesty.
